Fig1: Fig. 1 Normalization links test genes to estimated composition. a, Changes outside the marker panel alter a shared denominator, marker inputs and the adjusted expression coefficient. Marker-restricted normalization (MRN) uses the fixed marker-panel total as its denominator. b, Analytic sensitivity of log-transformed marker input to log denominator across marker-signal-to-pseudocount ratios. c, Input changes after denominator increases of 10%, 25% and 50%, with marker counts fixed. Curves follow the normalization transformation in Eq. (1)
Fig2: Fig. 2 Inferential changes under paired normalization controls. a, FDR with direct effects of 0.5 in 20 of 100 test genes. b, Coverage for the 80 unaffected genes. c, Proportion RMSE. Each condition used 80 mixtures of 200 nuclei and 200 repetitions per target donor. L-in and S-in denote six internal LIBD and SEA-AD targets; L-ext and S-ext denote the same 15 GSE174367 targets under the respective reference. Points are donor-equal means; whiskers are 95% Monte Carlo intervals conditional on donor banks. Dotted lines mark 5% FDR and 95% coverage. All planned tests were available
Fig3: Fig. 3 Pseudocount scale changes both denominator sensitivity and calibration. Panels a–d show L-in, S-in, L-ext and S-ext. Curves compare observed and paired fixed denominators at five pseudocount-to-scale ratios, with direct effects of 0.5 in 20 test genes. Points are donor-equal FDR estimates and whiskers are 95% Monte Carlo intervals. The response, sampled nuclei and test family are fixed within each paired comparison. The dotted line marks 5%. Donor banks and repetition counts follow Fig. 2
Fig4: Fig. 4 FDR and power across the relative-count marker grid. a, Paired MRN-minus-TMM FDR under the global null. b, Absolute MRN FDR. c, Paired power differences with 20 direct effects of 0.5. Columns cross within-class marker fractions of 5%, 10% and 20% with amplitudes 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0. Cells give donor-equal means in percent or percentage points (pp). Each scenario used 80 mixtures and 200 paired repetitions per donor. Marker quotas are specified in Online Resource 1, Section S4; paired intervals and availability appear in Online Resource 2, Table S4
Fig5: Fig. 5 Common-support allocation separates zero filling from persistent marker sensitivity. Panels a–d show L-in, S-in, L-ext and S-ext. Lines connect donor-equal global-null FDR under zero-allowing and positive-only allocation for predefined, reference-feature-matched and random subsets. Circles show TMM and squares show MRN; open symbols denote zero-allowing allocation and filled symbols denote positive-only allocation. Matched and random entries each average three fixed subsets within donor. Both support rules and all perturbed subsets share the same reduced sample-by-class count budget. Each unit used 50 repetitions; six internal or 15 external target donors contributed. The dotted line marks 5% FDR
Fig6: Fig. 6 Proportion RMSE and FDR across common-support marker subsets. Panels a–d show L-in, S-in, L-ext and S-ext under MRN and positive-only allocation. Each point is a donor-equal mean for one predefined, random or reference-feature-matched subset; the unperturbed control is shown separately. Three random and three matched subsets were used. All subsets share sampled nuclei, outcomes and reference inputs; perturbed subsets also share sample-by-class added-count totals. Each unit has 50 repetitions. The dotted line marks 5% global-null FDR
Fig7: Fig. 7 Marker restriction increases coefficient variation and reduces power in unperturbed mixtures. a,b, Power at effects 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 in the internal LIBD and SEA-AD settings. Whiskers are 95% Monte Carlo intervals. c, Composition-projection variance, noise-projection variance and twice their covariance for the 20 affected genes at effect 0.25 in SEA-AD. Diamonds give their sum, the coefficient-error variance. Components were calculated within gene over the same 200 repetitions and then averaged over genes and six target donors. d, Paired donor mean coefficients in that condition; large symbols give the donor-equal mean. All comparisons used 80 mixtures and returned all planned tests. Denom. denotes the denominator-only control
Fig8: Fig. 8 Clinical disease associations depend on composition-input normalization. a,b, TMM and MRN coefficients for the same 16,161 non-marker genes under LIBD and SEA-AD references. Colors indicate BH q ≤ 0.05 in both models, TMM only, MRN only or neither. c, Discoveries under five composition-input rules. Factor-only removes test genes from TMM factor estimation; complete exclusion also removes them from library totals. d, Empirical cumulative distributions of MRN-to-TMM standard-error ratios. All models use fixed responses, 288 fusiform-gyrus samples (218 Alzheimer disease, 70 control), age, sex and the common gene family. Retained marker counts are 152 for LIBD and 167 for SEA-AD
FigS1: Fig. S1 FDR and coverage with nonzero direct effects in the relative-count grid. a, MRN FDR. b, MRN coverage. c, MRN-minus-TMM coverage. Twenty test genes had direct effect 0.5. Cells show donor-equal means over 200 paired repetitions; settings and marker quotas follow Fig. 4
FigS2: Fig. S2 Common-support dose retention varies across settings and cell classes. a, Pooled retained fraction of requested counts in each setting, summed over 50 draws per target donor. b, Retention by marker class. Values are percentages of requested counts; classes follow the fixed marker assignments. Every subset and support rule receives the same retained sample-by-class budget. All 2,100 draws retain positive total budgets, although individual sample-by-class budgets may be zero
FigS3: Fig. S3 Denominator-only and full marker-restricted normalization have similar inferential performance. Panels show MRN-minus-denominator-only differences in global-null FDR, power with 20 direct effects of 0.25 and proportion RMSE under positive-only common-support allocation. Points are donor-equal contrasts for predefined subsets or the within-donor means of three matched or random subsets. Each unit used 50 paired repetitions. No confidence interval is represented by these descriptive points
FigS4: Fig. S4 Clinical disease alignment with the nuisance space. a, Disease-exposure R² against the nuisance space containing age, sex and estimated composition. b, Residualized-exposure sum of squares. Points compare the five composition-input rules under LIBD and SEA-AD references. All ten models have six composition contrasts and 16,161 available genes. Samples and disease labels are fixed
FigS5: Fig. S5 Donor-level marker associations in clinical single-nucleus data. Panels show owner-class log2 fold-change point estimates for the LIBD and SEA-AD panels in GSE174367. Primary models adjusted for age, source-recorded sex and batch. Each point is a testable marker; horizontal jitter separates points within class. Bars give class medians and dotted lines mark ±log2(1.5). No marker passed the planned-family BH threshold of 0.05. The candidate cohort contained 18 donors; class-specific eligibility is given in Online Resource 1, Section S7
FigS6: Fig. S6 Actual nuisance-span reporting separates estimability from a fixed-rank rule. The same MEAD point predictions and injected outcomes enter a rule requiring six composition contrasts and an actual-span rule. Panels show test availability, conditional coverage, delivered coverage and FDR with 20 direct effects of 0.5. Points give donor-equal means and whiskers give 95% Monte Carlo intervals over 200 repetitions per target. HC3 and leverage criteria are retained in both rules. Dotted lines mark 95% coverage or 5% FDR
Fig9: Fig. 9 Fixed-response perturbations isolate tested-gene normalization feedback. a,b, Fraction of the 16,161 clinical genes crossing q = 0.05 when tested-gene counts in AD samples are multiplied by exp(t) for composition-input construction, under LIBD and SEA-AD references. c,d, Root mean square coefficient change across the same genes. The horizontal axis gives the tested-count increase, 100[exp(t) − 1], for t = 0.01, 0.05 and 0.10. TMM and factor-only exclusion are shown separately. Complete exclusion, denominator-only normalization and MRN overlap at exactly zero throughout. Outcomes, marker counts, samples and the BH family are fixed; threshold crossings measure sensitivity rather than false discoveries
FigS7: Fig. S7 Local derivative reliability and numerical invariance. a, Planned, finite and qualified simulation diagnostic records per method and outcome; counts are identical across the two outcomes. Qualified scores in all five invariant arms are zero after the 10⁻⁶ floor. TMM and factor-only exclusion have no qualified records. b,c, Clinical relative derivative disagreement for TMM and factor-only exclusion under LIBD and SEA-AD references, across four central-difference steps. The dotted line is the qualification threshold of 0.1. These checks assess approximation reliability rather than FDR control
FigS8: Fig. S8 Fixed-response sensitivity under dtangle and MuSiC. a, b, Global-null outcomes. c, d, Twenty direct effects of 0.5 among 100 test genes. a, c, Additional counts in the disjoint tested-gene panel. b, d, Additional counts in the fixed marker subset. Outcomes, samples, references and the BH family remain fixed within each comparison. Points are donor-equal means of coefficient-change RMS; error bars show one conditional Monte Carlo standard error from 20 repetitions per reference-target unit. MuSiC uses its native raw-count processing, a fixed disjoint marker panel and native cell-fraction output. The four observed reference donors remain fixed across repetitions. L/S indicate LIBD/SEA-AD references; in/ext indicate internal/GSE174367 targets. Vertical scales differ between panels. Data: Table S16
